title: QVGen: Pushing the Limit of Quantized Video Generative Models
claim: Auxiliary modules cut quantization error to speed convergence, then are progressively decayed through low-rank truncation so inference cost returns to zero.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, zoom-in callout linking (a) to (b)
description: A two-panel method diagram. Panel (a), in a green dashed box on the left, shows how auxiliary modules improve convergence. A video frame with noise feeds a full-precision model and a quantized model, which are linked by a knowledge-distillation arrow. Below that is a quantized linear layer with weight W and quantized weight Q_b(W). A parallel auxiliary branch W_Φ adds its output to the main path at a sum node. A small loss-landscape sketch compares naive and 'ours' optimization paths, and a gradient-norm bound inequality sits beside it. Panel (b), on the right, is titled 'Progressively Shrinking Φ via Rank-Decay'. It shows W_Φ decomposed by SVD into L and R factors (orange and teal slabs), then truncated over stages with a cosine-annealed decay schedule. A gray callout cone links the two panels. A 'training time' arrow runs down the right edge. The eye goes first to the colored L and R blocks.

abstract: Video diffusion models (DMs) have enabled high-quality video synthesis. Yet, their substantial computational and memory demands pose serious challenges to real-world deployment, even on high-end GPUs. As a commonly adopted solution, quantization has proven notable success in reducing cost for image DMs, while its direct application to video DMs remains ineffective. In this paper, we present QVGen, a novel quantization-aware training (QAT) framework tailored for high-performance and inference-efficient video DMs under extremely low-bit quantization (e.g., 4-bit or below). We begin with a theoretical analysis demonstrating that reducing the gradient norm is essential to facilitate convergence for QAT. To this end, we introduce auxiliary modules ($Î¦$) to mitigate large quantization errors, leading to significantly enhanced convergence. To eliminate the inference overhead of $Î¦$, we propose a rank-decay strategy that progressively eliminates $Î¦$. Specifically, we repeatedly employ singular value decomposition (SVD) and a proposed rank-based regularization $\mathbfÎ³$ to identify and decay low-contributing components. This strategy retains performance while zeroing out additional inference overhead. Extensive experiments across $4$ state-of-the-art (SOTA) video DMs, with parameter sizes ranging from $1.3\text{B}\sim14\text{B}$, show that QVGen is the first to reach full-precision comparable quality under 4-bit settings. Moreover, it significantly outperforms existing methods. For instance, our 3-bit CogVideoX-2B achieves improvements of $+25.28$ in Dynamic Degree and $+8.43$ in Scene Consistency on VBench. Code and models are available at https://github.com/ModelTC/QVGen.
